question: Who is the author of the book 'The Namesake'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jhumpa Lahiri**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri** is the author of the novel **"The Namesake"**, which was published in **2003**. 
 
• The book explores themes of **identity, cultural assimilation, and the immigrant experience**, particularly focusing on the life of a Bengali family in the United States. 
 
• **"The Namesake"** is Jhumpa Lahiri's first novel, following her Pulitzer Prize-winning short story collection **"Interpreter of Maladies" (1999)**. 
 
• The protagonist of the novel, **Gogol Ganguli**, struggles to reconcile his Indian heritage with his American upbringing, making the book a poignant tale of identity and belonging. 
 
• A film adaptation of **"The Namesake"**, directed by **Mira Nair**, was released in **2006**, further popularizing the book. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

 
 
• **Jhumpa Lahiri's Background:** 
 
 
• Jhumpa Lahiri was born in **London** to Bengali parents and later moved to the **United States**. 
 
• She is known for her exploration of themes related to **diaspora, identity, and family dynamics**. 
 
• Lahiri has received numerous accolades, including the **Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 2000** for her debut short story collection "Interpreter of Maladies." 
 
 
 
• **About "The Namesake":** 
 
 
• The title **"The Namesake"** refers to the protagonist's name, **Gogol**, which holds cultural and emotional significance for his family. 
 
• The novel addresses the complexities of **intergenerational and cross-cultural relationships**. 
 
• It is considered a modern classic and is often studied in literature courses for its exploration of immigrant identity. 
 
 
 
• **Other Works by Jhumpa Lahiri:** 
 
 
• **"Interpreter of Maladies" (1999):** A collection of short stories that earned her the Pulitzer Prize. 
 
• **"Unaccustomed Earth" (2008):** Another acclaimed collection of short stories. 
 
• **"In Other Words" (2016):** A memoir written in Italian, reflecting her love for the language and culture of Italy. 
 
 
 
• **Other Options:** 
 
 
• **Arundhati Roy:** Author of "The God of Small Things," which won the Booker Prize in 1997. 
 
• **Satyajit Ray:** Renowned filmmaker and writer, known for his Feluda series in Bengali literature. 
 
• **Arun Joshi:** Known for novels like "The Strange Case of Billy Biswas" and "The Apprentice."
